episodes.168713: As an area of high pressure remained centered to the east of New Mexico, it allowed for a healthy stream of moisture to continue to move into the western half of the state on June 18, 2022. With the monsoonal moisture plume focused in this area, the day's thunderstorms favored areas along and west of the central mountain chain. With moisture streaming into the area over the past few days, the atmosphere was primed and better able to support thunderstorms with heavy rain. One of these thunderstorms near Embudo in Rio Arriba County produced an estimated 1.5 to 2.5 inches of rain which caused flooding along area roadways. Another washed out a section of New Mexico State Road 6 near Los Lunas, forcing the closure of the highway.
episodes.168920: A Pacific trough and associated cold front moved through the area.  This feature would trigger strong and severe thunderstorms, mainly during the overnight hours.
episodes.169023: A strong dust devil developed and moved in an urbanized sector of Fortuna Foothills just east of Yuma, causing extensive property damage. There were social media images of roofs torn off, roofing tiles blown off, brick wall collapsing, trees uprooted, and massive debris hitting power lines, knocking power out to 2022 customers. No injuries were reported.
episodes.169033: Deep southerly flow brought sufficient instability and shear to the region. An approaching trough provided sufficient forcing for ascent, resulting in a few severe thunderstorms across western portions of North-central Montana. One supercell dominated, beginning near Lincoln, travelling northeastward, finally crossing the Canadian border at the Blaine/Hill County border.
episodes.169200: A thunderstorm became severe over Ziebach County, producing wind gusts to 60 mph in the Dupree area.
episodes.169201: A supercell thunderstorm developed over far northern Campbell County and tracked northeast into southeastern Montana. The storm produced large hail near Rockypoint.
episodes.169203: A cluster of thunderstorms briefly became severe over northern Jackson County, producing some wind gusts over 60 mph.
episodes.169287: With the high pressure center to the east of New Mexico, a steady plume of moisture was present across western New Mexico on June 19, 2022. With these large moisture values, it was an active monsoon day across the area with scattered to numerous thunderstorms favored areas west of the central mountains. Cibola County was hit hardest as severe thunderstorms dropped large hail, and heavy rain caused flash flooding.
episodes.169349: The presence of monsoon moisture paired with the passing of a trough aloft led to widespread showers and thunderstorms across western Colorado. Several storms produced heavy rain. Additionally, severe thunderstorms produced large hail and strong winds in across some areas.
episodes.169543: Afternoon thunderstorms produce wind damage near Wildwood in Sumter County.
episodes.169544: Afternoon sea breeze thunderstorms produce gusty winds over the coastal waters.
episodes.169910: An isolated severe thunderstorm produced some large hail and strong winds.
episodes.169929: A thunderstorm dropped one-inch diameter hail at Herman on the evening of the 19th.
episodes.170218: A couple rounds of thunderstorms developed in the vicinity of an elongated area of low pressure during the evening of the 19th across central South Dakota, and then tracked north-northeast. Straight-line wind gusts of 60 to 70 mph were produced, including at three miles south of Bunker (70 mph), and five miles west-southwest of Mound City (70 mph).
episodes.170222: A slow-moving cold front pushed into NE FL, just beyond the GA/FL line, and nearly stalled in the afternoon. Scattered showers and storms developed south of the boundary in the early afternoon. Dry air and steep lapse rates aloft fueled a few strong to severe storms which produced downburst winds.
episodes.170501: A shortwave moving across Wyoming brought high wind gusts to portions of central Wyoming.
episodes.170547: Strong to severe thunderstorms developed in a very moist and unstable air mass across eastern Oklahoma on the 18th, as a weak frontal boundary moved into the area from the east and northeast. The strongest thunderstorms produced damaging wind gusts.
episodes.171198: A potent upper level disturbance initially brought showers and thunderstorms to the region, but transitioned to a more stratiform event that produced many heavy rain reports.
episodes.171202: An isolated thunderstorm became severe across South Lake Charles.
episodes.171207: On June 19th, afternoon thunderstorms developed in east-central Colorado due to a surface trough setting up on the lee side of the Rocky Mountains. One of these thunderstorms produced a wind gust up to an estimated 65 mph.
episodes.171413: A couple of strong storms produced small hail and gusty winds in parts of North Texas the afternoon of Sunday, June 19.
episodes.171463: A few decaying showers and storms produced some high wind gusts in Huerfano and Pueblo County on June 19th.
episodes.171554: A low pressure trough over South Florida and the development of afternoon sea breezes led to thunderstorms over metro Southeast Florida, producing strong wind gusts and small hail.
episodes.171569: A weak convective storm produced a cold core funnel.
episodes.171713: A widespread high wind event across Utah was followed by strong thunderstorms associated with a system spanning a three-day period. These storms produced numerous instances of severe wind gusts, in addition to a tornado, a report of hail, and flash flooding.

events.narrative: Heavy rain near Los Lunas caused a section of New Mexico State Road 6 to wash out. One vehicle with a family of three was traveling on the roadway when the road was washed out. Their car was submerged, but fortunately, nearby contruction workers were able to pull the family out of the car. No injuries were reported. The flooding forced the closure of the roadway during the evening hours. Damages are estimated.
The spotter estimated wind gusts around 60 mph.
A power line was downed in town by the wind.

A strong dust devil developed and moved northward in an urbanized sector of Fortuna Foothills just east of Yuma, causing extensive property damage. There were social media images of roofs torn off, roofing tiles blown off, a brick wall collapsing, trees uprooted and massive debris hitting power lines, knocking power out to 2022 customers. The dust devil tracked northward between 10E and 36th Street and South Payson Drive to South Fontage Road near I-8. No injuries were reported.

A tornado developed near the summit of US-191 and Argyle Canyon |Road in remote southwestern Duchesne County at about 9200 feet. |Sporadic damage is noted in this area as it moved north over a |ridge line and into a valley adjacent to US-191 along Indian |Canyon.||The tornado then descended down the length of the valley from |about 9200 feet to a creek adjacent to US-191 at an elevation of |about 8500 feet. Over this period, both the strength and and width|of the tornado increased substantially with a continuous damage |path through a mixed aspen and conifer forest. The maximum damage |was found in this area and was significant. Almost all trees over |a large hillside facing the road were violently blown down, |snapped, or topped into a clearly convergent axis. Several tree |tops were desposited along the creek and road with no clear |indicatation as to where they orginated.||The tornado then crossed US-191 and ascended the hillside from |about 8500 feet to another ridge on the northwest side of the road|to an elevation of about 9100 feet. Considerable damage was noted|immediately north of US-191 where numerous trees were snapped or |uprooted, although not to the severe extent noted on the south |side of the road. Damage decreased considerably up the hillside to|the top of the 9100 foot ridge line with more sporadic toppled |trees.||A few toppled trees were noted into the next basin over the ridge|on the north side of the road, marking the last discernible |damage from the tornado, and the end of the 2 mile damage path.
